title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This page centralizes platform engineering systems and services documentation for the Platform team. It combines a concise systems inventory, practical how-tos for on-call and operations, dashboard and alerting patterns, canonical runbooks, a short retrospective summary of recent reliability work, and the near-term roadmap. Use this as the canonical team wiki landing page for day-to-day ops and onboarding.

Scope

- Services covered: routing, API-gateway, request-queue, batching-service, cache-service, model-proxy, autoscaler, metrics-ingest, tracing-collector, deployment-orchestrator.
- Environments: prod, prod-canary, staging, dev.
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, incident responders, solutions engineers working on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Ownership and contacts

- Platform systems owner: Platform Systems (team)
- Primary on-call rotation: platform-sre-oncall (see paging rota)
- Pager escalation: oncall -> platform-ice (escalation lead) -> platform-ops-manager -> CTO on critical P1s
- Slack channel: #platform-ops (primary), #platform-incidents (postmortem comms)

How-tos (quick operational recipes)

1) New service onboarding checklist

- Create service page in team wiki with: owners, runbook, SLOs, dashboard links, deployment runbook.
- Add Prometheus metrics: request_rate, error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_depth, worker_count.
- Create standard Grafana dashboard (use template: platform-service-overview) and attach to runbook.
- Configure alerts (see Alerts section) and add to ops rotation.
- Add service to capacity planning spreadsheet and weekly capacity sync.

2) Creating a new dashboard (step-by-step)

- Copy the platform-service-overview dashboard from the dashboard library.
- Replace datasource with metrics-store:prod and update metric names to the new service prefix.
- Panels to include: Request rate, Error rate (4xx/5xx split), Latency histogram, Backend pool utilization, Queue depth, Recent errors log (links).
- Set panel thresholds consistent with SLOs and export dashboard JSON to the service runbook.

3) Deploying a non-breaking config change to autoscaler

- Create branch and open PR referencing the autoscaler playbook.
- Run unit + integration tests in staging; confirm metrics & scaling behavior via synthetic load.
- Schedule a low-traffic canary window (prod-canary) and monitor: queue_depth, p95_latency, worker_spinup_time.
- Roll forward if stable; rollback if p95 latency increases > 15% or error rate spike > 2x baseline.

Dashboards & alerts — patterns and thresholds

SLOs and Error Budgets

- Default availability SLO for platform telemetry: service-level availability 99.9% monthly (unless otherwise specified).
- Latency SLOs defined per service (see inventory table).
- Error budget burn is reviewed weekly in SRE sync; aggressive mitigations triggered at 25% remaining error budget.

Alerting taxonomy

- Severity P1 (page): service-down, total request failure (>5m sustained 50%+ error rate), critical security events.
- Severity P2 (page + Slack): high latency impacting SLOs (p99 > threshold for 10m), queue backlog growth > 3x baseline for 15m.
- Severity P3 (Slack): rising error rate anomalies, degraded metrics (partial failures), config drift warnings.

Recommended thresholds (examples)

- api-gateway: p99 latency > 800ms for 10m -> P2; 5xx rate > 2% sustained 5m -> P1.
- request-queue: queue_depth > 1000 for 10m -> P2; message loss detected -> P1.
- batching-service: p95 batching latency > 300ms for 5m -> P2.

Alert fatigue mitigation

- Use anomaly detection for noise-prone metrics (e.g., model-specific error spikes).
- Configure alert deduplication and route noisy alerts to a separate Slack channel for triage.
- Review alert firing history monthly and adjust thresholds.

Canonical runbooks (high-level excerpts)

1) High-level incident response (standard operating procedure)

1.1 Triage
- Acknowledge the page within 2 minutes.
- Determine scope: service(s) impacted, regions, customer impact.
- Assign incident commander (IC) and scribe.

1.2 Contain
- Apply quick circuit breakers: mute downstream consumers, toggle feature flags, divert traffic to canary region.
- If model stalls/blocking, disable batching and fall back to passthrough to shorter timeouts.

1.3 Mitigate
- Scale up worker pool (manual override) if autoscaler lagging.
- Revert recent config/deployments if correlated (use deployment-orchestrator history).

1.4 Recovery & Post-incident
- Restore normal traffic gradually.
- Capture timeline, root cause hypotheses, and action items in postmortem document within 72 hours.

2) Runbook: High API latency (example)

- Step 1: Check global SLO dashboard and determine which services show latency (api-gateway vs batching-service).
- Step 2: If api-gateway is the bottleneck, check ingress pods, CPU/memory, and request_rate. Scale if pods at 90% CPU.
- Step 3: If batching-service shows high p99, temporarily reduce batch_size via runtime flag and monitor p50/p95.
- Step 4: If autoscaler is slow to react, perform manual scale and file infra ticket.

Retrospectives and recent initiatives

- Q4 2027 retro summary: Reworked autoscaler heuristics and introduced conservative cold-start buffering. Result: 35% reduction in P2 incidents related to scale-up lag and 12% lower median latency under burst traffic.
- Action items completed: standardized platform-service-overview dashboard, added queue-length based autoscaling policy, updated runbook templates.
- Ongoing: continued work on prefix cache eviction policies and KV cache observability.

Roadmap (next 6 months)

- M1 (Mar 2028): Roll out cross-region fallback routing for API-gateway; objective: reduce region-specific P1s by 50%.
- M2 (Apr 2028): Deploy metrics-store autoscaler and reduce ingestion lag under peak by 70%.
- M3 (May 2028): Launch platform runbook automation (playbooks that can execute safe remediation steps via runbook-bot).
- M4 (Jun 2028): Onboard Dedicated customer clusters into centralized dashboards and SLO reporting.
